newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin sells off edible oils producer.
newsitem.headline: Benin sells off edible oils producer.

text.p: Benin has sold off SONICOG, a state-owned producer of edible oils, butter and soap, to Swiss, Ivorian and local interests for a total of 5.04 billion CFA francs ($8.7 million), the denationalisation committee said on Monday.

Ivory Coast's SIFCA, principally a coffee and cocoa exporter, bought a mixed oil-producing factory for two billion CFA francs, while Aiglon, a Swiss company, paid 1.9 billion for a palmoil production plant plus a soap-making unit.
A Benin import-export company, Aboussi Odoumare, bought another palmoil plant for 1.1 billion CFA francs.
The state had tried on four occasions between 1993 and 1996 to sell SONICOG as a single concern, before the government finally agreed to accept bids for parts of the firm.

One condition of the sale was that the new owners had to employ all the 870 workers currently employed by the state firm, the head of the denationalisation committee, Celestine Zanou-Wetohossou, told Reuters.
This is the eighth privatisation in Benin since 1990, and in total the sales have generated about 20 billion CFA francs for the state.
The government has lined up petroleum products company SONACOP as the next firm to be privatised. ($ = 580 CFA francs)
